Voice review needs help. I have been using the voice recognition feature to review verses for a few years. The concept is great. But it just doesn’t work out very well. When I started, it was ok. It sometimes couldn’t figure out a word when I said it. But I could add a substitute. This worked out well for KJV. Because the app would assume that I wanted modern words, I could substitute one that it thought I was saying for the correct one. But then came some updates to the app I wish I never installed them. The voice recognition would no longer store all the words I spoke. It would drop some out entirely. Especially when there were verses with the same word at the beginning of each short phrase. Like phl4:8nkjv. Then the app would assume I was stuttering and drop entire phrases and wait for me to repeat them. 
Then came version 9.0 and I thought maybe they fixed it. Boy was I wrong. The same problems still exist but now they added a new, may I call it a bug. Now the app marks words as wrong if it doesn’t recognized that you said them correctly. Often it takes one syllable and inserts 2 or three words marked wrong. I would try the verses over and over, but no matter how I would pause between each word or say something that was obviously shorter than the word it was waiting for, it would insert 3 words and mark them all wrong. I just tried prov3:5-6 kjv. and it couldn’t figure out the word unto. It would insert multiple words when I would make the slightest sound for unto. 
I think the biggest feature that we need for voice review is to be able to remove exceptions that were accidentally added. This is to teach the app what it is we are saying when it hurts stuck. And the next is to be able to reassign a word after the app inserted the wrong one. This is a separate feature to tell the app that it was confidently wrong and wast it should have heard. As humans we take the context into account to help us discern what someone is saying. The app needs to do that too. Don’t suggest exercise if the verse is Latin and has the word excelsis. Well maybe it can’t do Latin. But it should be able to do KJV and NKJV and NASB without suggesting it heard curse words or explicit vocabulary. By all means it has the verse to compare with. It knows the vocabulary to pick from. Let it use that vocabulary. Let it even favor it.

reviews.text: DOWNLOAD THISSS :). The free/lite version works 100% if you want to memorize verses, the way they made the app is super smart. Basically, you type in the first letter of each word and then it will show the verse with half the words missing so you type the first letter of the missing word and it fills it in with red letters if incorrect and regular black color if correct. It will give you an accuracy percentage each time you attempt the verse. If you do not get 100% it will continue to test you, for example it will show you the verse with half the words missing again, but this time the words that were not missing the first time you tried and the ones that were missing will be shown. There are zero ads (even with the lite/free version), and I would like to thank the developers for that. You still learn exactly as you would with the paid version using lite, the only difference is you can read the scripture in the app with paid as well as see advanced statistics on your learning habits rather than basic charts. I memorized three verses within ~ 30/40 minutes. And I *really* memorized them. Not just memorized but only retained the information temporarily. BEST Scripture Memory App!. I’ve been using the Pro version of this app for almost 10 years and it has been a huge blessing. In so many ways. Though the free version is fine, it doesn’t enable you to enjoy the best features. Totally worth it to pay the one time fee of less than $10.

What I LOVE about it: (in no particular order)

• I can use multiple translations of verses, which is great if you’ve memorized verses in the past in different translations that you want to add to the app to review (or relearn)

•It includes so many translations, including both the current NIV and the 1984 version, which is helpful if you memorized verses in the older version.

•You can easily import the text.

•You can group the verses by topic.

• I can record myself saying them and play them back at the speed I want and repeat as much as I want which is great for driving, walking, etc. 

• There are flash cards available, which is helpful 

• The system for learning is great, because it has three levels for memorizing each verse, all only typing the first letter of each word: 
Level 1: starts with the whole verse set where you can see and you type over it. You can repeat this until you’re ready for the next level. Level 2: every other word is missing, and as you complete your review, it alternates whether it’s the first or second word that is missing. You can repeat this level until you’re ready for a blank space.
Level 3: you type the whole verse (all of this is first letters only) At this level, you earn points for memorizing and reviewing.

•If points motivate you, you get the most points for 100% on your first try. You can set the proficiency level to what you want.

• There are a lot of badges for when you first start. I do wish there were more of these after earning most of them in the first six months, it was kind of disappointing that there weren’t new incentives. But the real reward is hiding God’s Word in my heart and how it helps me pray and think God’s thoughts after Him.

• You can turn on the microphone and recite the verse by speaking instead of typing. (Maybe it’s my accent, but I find I often have to repeat myself or say the same word over and over to get it to register some of the time. That is a little frustrating because part of reviewing is getting the whole thing at once. But it is still a helpful feature.)

•You can easily share verse with others.

I’m sure there is much more I’m forgetting. Bottom line: if you want to memorize God’s Word and shouldn’t we all??? this app is a wonderful tool!

Awesome!!. I have used this app for years and love it. I have been a maximum security prison chaplain for 30 years and speaking memorized verses is an amazing ministry tool to reach people. So, I like to memorize whole chapters and edit the Bible translation of choice to amplify certain key Hebrew or Greek words so the people I minister to really get those key words. Most apps confine me to importing a single English Bible translation and make me use it as is, but this app allows me to paste in my edited/amplified version so I can memorize exactly strategically expanded key words. I can also use my own voice to record so I can put in pauses and listen to the passages with real feeling so I memorize it that way. This isn’t about just memorizing and speaking it fast and without feeling. It’s about conveying God’s love and truth in a relational and impactful way. So, this app allows me to really design where to pause and what to emphasize, etc. Great syncing, never really had a problem, and I think that covers it all. Highly recommend.

Really like it so far. I’ve only had this app for a day but I’m already impressed. Sure, there are features I’d love to have that are not in the free version, but I’m also a believer in paying workers what they’re worth, so I don’t begrudge them keeping some features only in the paid version. Anyway, I was looking for an app that would make memorization more fun and easier than my old-fashioned way of just repeatedly reading and writing, which wasn’t working anyway. It gets a whole lot harder to memorize as we age, but the method of tapping the first letter of each word, then gradually having more words removed, is really effective. It’s also kind of fun, more like a game than work. So I’m more likely to open this app and practice verses than I am to scroll social media when I have spare time.
